description: What Excel does to a data table when a splice deletes its input cell. A one-variable column table at A3:B6 over the input cell D1 was built over COM, and the input cell was then deleted three ways in three copies: its row, its column, and the cell alone with the cells below shifting up. Each copy's B4 formula was read back and each was saved.
probe: test/corpus/fixtures/data-table-input-cell-deleted/author.ps1 for the committed pair; a one-off COM script covering all three deletions

saved.before: <c r="B4"><f t="dataTable" ref="B4:B6" dt2D="0" dtr="0" r1="D1"/><v>2</v></c>
saved.row 1 deleted: <c r="B3" t="e"><f t="dataTable" ref="B3:B5" dt2D="0" dtr="0" del1="1" r1="D1"/><v>#REF!</v></c>
saved.column D deleted: <c r="B4" t="e"><f t="dataTable" ref="B4:B6" dt2D="0" dtr="0" del1="1" r1="D1"/><v>#REF!</v></c>

verdict: Excel keeps the input reference exactly as it was written and flags it deleted with del1 (del2 for the second input of a two-variable table), whichever way the cell goes; the table's own range moves with the grid, and its cells show #REF!.
